title: Blood pressure-lowering treatment based on cardiovascular risk: a meta-analysis of individual patient data
authors: Blood Pressure Lowering Treatment Trialists' Collaboration
population: Individual participant data from 11 trials (26 randomised groups, 67,475 individuals) of blood-pressure-lowering drugs against placebo or of more against less intensive regimens; 51,917 with data for the risk equations, grouped by predicted 5-year cardiovascular risk (<11%, 11 to 15%, 15 to 21%, >21%)
funder: Funding: None (as stated in the published summary; the full text with the role and declaration sections is behind a subscription).
result: 4167 participants (8%) had a cardiovascular event. Mean predicted 5-year risks in the four groups were 6.0%, 12.1%, 17.7% and 26.8%. Relative reductions in cardiovascular events were 18% (95% CI 7 to 27), 15% (4 to 25), 13% (2 to 22) and 15% (5 to 24) (p for trend 0.30). Treating 1000 patients for 5 years would prevent 14 (8 to 21), 20 (8 to 31), 24 (8 to 40) and 38 (16 to 61) cardiovascular events respectively (p for trend 0.04).
